newsitem.title: BELARUS: Skoda on track to build cars in Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Skoda on track to build cars in Belarus.

text.p: Volkswagen AG's Czech automaker Skoda automobilova AS is set to remove obstacles to its plans to build as many as 5,000 vehicles a year in a $20 million project in Belarus, the country's Minister for Foreign Economic Relations Mikhail Marinich said.

"Two questions remain," Marinich said. "The first is the package of investment incentives, which the government must decide. And the second is the location of the production, which Skoda must decide."
"I think we will solve these questions by September," he added. "And the size of the possible investment could be $20 million with the aim to build 5,000 Skoda Felicia cars a year."

The government is considering granting to Skoda similar concessions that Ford Motor Co received for a $19.2 million project to assemble Escort cars and Transit commercial vehicles, which will officially start operations on July 30.
"We are negotiating with Skoda to offer the same kind of support that we have provided to Ford," Marinich said. "And we think that they are eligible for the same privileges as Ford."

He did not elaborate, but Ford said it received a five-year exemption on corporate profit tax and an indefinite allowance for duty-free imports of plant equipment and material as well as the kits of car bodies and parts that Ford will assemble in Belarus.

Skoda said earlier that it encountered difficulties in negotiating a deal, and the assistant to Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko told journalists visiting Minsk this week that Skoda's original investment proposal was too self-serving and small to merit the same treatment given to Ford.

"Our advice (to Skoda) was to make a draft agreement between Skoda and Belarus similar to the agreement between Ford and Belarus," Piotr Kapitula, the assistant, said. "Then the issue will be resolved, and Skoda will be produced on the same conditions as Ford."

"The two-year term project that was (originally) presented to us was just a commercial project where one can gain much money and abandon the market -- that's all," he added. "That is why it was not examined by the presidential administration."
Skoda could not be reached immediately to comment on their investment plans in Belarus.

Regarding the investment's location, Skoda has been examining a site in Dzjarzynsk, roughly 40 km (25 miles) southwest of Minsk. The government also has invited the Czech automaker to consider investing in the customs-free zone in Brest, near the Polish border in southwest Belarus.
Belarus only sells a few thousand new vehicles a year, but Skoda has said it would export most of the cars it assembles to Russia.
Skoda has also been negotiating to assemble Felicias in Russia in Smolensk, roughly 70 km (45 miles) east of northern Belarus.

"We are considering three options in the former Soviet Union -- assembly in Belarus or Russia or both," a Skoda official told Reuters last week, noting the company expects to sell over 12,000 vehicles in Russia this year.
